calibration.purpose: Same-store fixed-capacity case design with an industrially balanced workbench capacity c=18: s, m, q_j, h_j, SKU pool, item_sizes, and c are identical for Normal, Busy, and Peak; only n and the corresponding prefix of the same order-demand stream differ.
calibration.scenario_description: Normal demand volume under the same fixed physical store capacity; only n changes.
calibration.notes: SKU category and demand shares are used only to generate/describe the anonymized order-SKU demand data. The optimization model uses orders/o_i,k, item_sizes/w_k, zone_capacities/h_j, workbench_capacity/c, and picker_capacity/q_j. picker_capacity is retained for code compatibility and should be interpreted as q_j.

case_generation_rule.sku_id_convention: SKU IDs are used as zero-based indices, consistent with the original JSON statistics.
case_generation_rule.note: Normal and Busy use the first n orders from the same anonymized demand stream; Peak uses all 500 orders. The same c=18, s=1500, m=6, q_j, and h_j are used in all three cases.

calibration.workbench_capacity_design_note: The workbench capacity is set to c=18 rather than c=36 to represent a medium-size instant-retail consolidation bench. This setting remains operationally realistic while making the continuous replenishment and task-allocation decisions non-trivial; it is not an extreme stress-test setting.
